explanation: The head is considered the most sacred part of the body in Thailand, believed to be where the spirit resides, so touching or patting anyone's head, including a child's, is seen as deeply disrespectful. This applies regardless of hierarchy or age; even masseuses typically ask permission before touching a client's head. Close family touching a young child's head is the main accepted exception.
local_tip: Keep your hands away from anyone's head and hair, no matter how friendly the gesture feels to you — use a light touch on the arm or shoulder instead if you need their attention.

also_check.note: Touching the head is usually avoided out of respect, especially for elders.
Touching someone's head without permission is seen as invasive, since personal space is highly valued.
A pat on a child's head is often read as affectionate, though doing it to an adult can seem condescending.

sources.title: Feet Low, Head High: A Guide to Thai Etiquettes
